solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Little European aquatic larva (7)

annotation.surface: A zoology note about some small creature from a European pond.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pulls Little and European together as description of the larva; in fact each word is its own building block.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the young of a frog or toad lives in water as a larva before it grows legs.

entries.clue: Get to grips with heavy lifting equipment (6)

blocks.note: the ropes and pulleys used for hoisting

annotation.surface: Someone learning to handle a crane or hoist.
annotation.walkthrough: Tackle is both a verb for confronting something and a noun for the rigging used to lift loads, as in block and tackle.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: the verb sense is confronting a problem, the noun sense is the ropes and pulleys of a hoist.

entries.clue: Father catches eastern vessel, giving nothing away (7)

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so Father holds the E inside him

blocks.note: a pan is a cooking vessel

annotation.surface: A father grabbing an oriental pot while keeping a poker face.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma splits the wordplay from the definition, which reads like a comment on Father's expression.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a face or delivery showing no emotion reveals nothing of what the speaker thinks.

entries.clue: Latin once translated at regular intervals (9)

indicators.note: translating changes the form of the words, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A schoolroom memory of Latin passages that used to be translated regularly.
annotation.walkthrough: Translated sits naturally with Latin, which hides its role as the anagram indicator. The definition is loose: octennial means every eight years, one particular regular interval.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by generalisation: something recurring every eight years happens at a fixed, regular interval.

entries.clue: Like the Golden Hind, ablaze in the works? (11)

indicators.note: in the works = being processed, so the letters are worked into a new order

annotation.surface: Francis Drake's ship on fire in a shipyard.
annotation.walkthrough: The Golden Hind was Sir Francis Drake's ship. The phrase in the works reads as one idiom, but in the belongs to the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by association: Drake sailed her round the world under Elizabeth I, so she belongs to that reign.

entries.clue: Move unsteadily over river, one in southern Africa (7)

blocks.note: the Po is the river of northern Italy

annotation.surface: Someone staggering across a river somewhere in southern Africa.
annotation.walkthrough: River looks like part of the definition, but it gives PO; the definition is one in southern Africa, the one being a river like the Po.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this river rises near Johannesburg and flows to the Indian Ocean through Mozambique.

entries.clue: Priest delaying start of Easter Story (3)

indicators.note: to delay something is to put it off, so the E is held back until after the rest
the start of Easter is its first letter, E, the same E that begins the priest

blocks.note: Eli, the priest who raised Samuel, a crossword regular, with his E held back
the E, first letter of Easter, moved to the end

annotation.surface: A priest putting off the first telling of the Easter story.
annotation.walkthrough: The E at the start of ELI is also the start of Easter; delaying it to the back turns the priest into the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the sense of telling stories: an untruth.

entries.clue: Paltry to confine good woman in Llandaff, perhaps (5)

indicators.note: to confine is to shut something in, so the word for paltry encloses the G

annotation.surface: A stingy attempt to lock up a virtuous woman in a Welsh town.
annotation.walkthrough: Llandaff is a district of Cardiff in Wales, and Megan is a typically Welsh girl's name; perhaps flags the definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Regional definition by example: a common Welsh first name, so a woman one might meet in a Welsh town.

entries.clue: Wind instrument, kind mostly found in orchestra’s wings (7)

indicators.note: most of CARING, dropping its last letter
CARIN sits inside the outer letters
the wings of a word are its outer letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of orchestra
CARING (kind) without its last letter, placed between O and A

annotation.surface: A wind player tucked away at the edges of the orchestra.
annotation.walkthrough: Wings suggests the side stage of a theatre; here it means the two ends of the word orchestra.
annotation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument.

entries.clue: Unacceptable appointments for distant territories (8)

blocks.note: out = not acceptable, as in that's out

annotation.surface: Complaints about undesirable postings to faraway colonies.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is of officials refusing jobs in remote places, which is roughly what the answer means anyway.
annotation.definitionFit: Outposts are remote settlements or territories far from the centre.

entries.clue: Begin to fish outside old country’s boundary (9)

indicators.note: outside places the phrase for beginning to fish around the letter for old

blocks.note: to cast a line is how an angler starts fishing
O = old, placed after the C

annotation.surface: An angler starting to fish just beyond some old frontier.
annotation.walkthrough: Begin looks like a first-letter indicator for fish, but the whole phrase is the charade CAST LINE.
annotation.definitionFit: A coastline is the boundary of a country where it meets the sea.

entries.clue: Shoot service personnel in luxury car (5)

indicators.note: in puts the service personnel inside the car, as passengers sit in it

blocks.note: GT = gran turismo, a grand touring car
the Royal Air Force, one of the services

annotation.surface: Airmen being gunned down inside a sports car.
annotation.walkthrough: Shoot reads as a verb of violence; here it is the gardener's noun, a cutting.
annotation.definitionFit: A graft is a shoot inserted into another plant to grow on it.

entries.clue: Blooming thing, much like a wolf (5)

indicators.note: much of the word, not all: the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A blooming nuisance of a thing, behaving like a wolf.
annotation.walkthrough: Blooming reads as a mild British swear word, as in blooming nuisance; it really means flowering. The flower's name does in fact come from the Latin for wolf.
annotation.definitionFit: The lupin is a flowering garden plant.

entries.clue: An Italian poet, endlessly in love, moving at a gentle pace (9)

indicators.note: the poet's name loses its last letter

blocks.note: love = zero in tennis, so O

annotation.surface: Dante strolling along, forever in love.
annotation.walkthrough: In love looks like a container instruction, but IN and O simply follow on in order.
annotation.definitionFit: Andantino is the musical direction for a moderately gentle, walking pace.

entries.clue: Detachment dig up English street (11)

annotation.surface: A military detachment ordered to dig up an English street.
annotation.walkthrough: Detachment reads as a squad of soldiers; the definition is the other sense, impartiality.
annotation.definitionFit: Disinterest means impartial detachment, having no stake in the outcome.

entries.clue: Somehow it’s apparent in summer, ultimately preventing sweat (14)

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in some other way
take the last letter of summer

blocks.note: the last letter of summer, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A remark that somehow it's obvious in summer why you'd want to stop sweating.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is barely disguised: the scene is summer sweat, and the answer is what you'd reach for.
annotation.definitionFit: Antiperspirant, as an adjective, describes something that prevents sweating.

entries.clue: Like some twins broadcasting in dialect (9)

indicators.note: the letters are scattered, as seed is broadcast

annotation.surface: Twin presenters on local radio speaking in their regional accent.
annotation.walkthrough: In dialect looks like a phrase attached to broadcasting, but in is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Identical twins come from one egg and look alike.

entries.clue: Initially employing second vehicle, obtained food in Paris (8)

indicators.note: take the first letter of employing

annotation.surface: Hiring a second car to go and fetch dinner in Paris.
annotation.walkthrough: In Paris signals a French word: escargot is French for snail, eaten as a delicacy.
annotation.definitionFit: Escargot, a snail, is classic French food.

entries.clue: Unaided, run part of body finally based in Cambs city (6-8)

indicators.note: take the last letter of based
the D is housed inside ELY

blocks.note: in cricket a single is one run
a hand is a body part
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire (Cambs)
last letter of based, placed inside ELY

annotation.surface: Someone running a business alone from a base in a Cambridgeshire city.
annotation.walkthrough: Cambs is the usual abbreviation for Cambridgeshire, an English county, and Ely is the small cathedral city in it that setters use constantly.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something single-handedly means doing it unaided.

entries.clue: Molluscs identified by mischievous falsehood on radio (7)

indicators.note: what the radio listener hears, not reads

annotation.surface: Sea creatures unmasked by a cheeky fib told on air.
annotation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech naughty lie and nautili sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: Nautili, plural of nautilus, are shelled cephalopod molluscs.

entries.clue: Tolerant knight that is taken in fast (7)

indicators.note: N and IE are taken inside LENT

blocks.note: Lent is the Christian fast before Easter

annotation.surface: A forbearing knight who has been swallowed up quickly.
annotation.walkthrough: Fast reads as quickly; it is the religious fast, Lent.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone mild in judging others tolerates what a stricter person would punish.

entries.clue: Possibly collect sportsperson changing sides almost at the start (6)

indicators.note: L (left) is swapped for R (right)
the swap is in the second letter, nearly the first

blocks.note: a player takes part in a sport

blocks.clueFragment: changing sides almost at the start
blocks.note: L becomes R in the second position

annotation.surface: An athlete switching teams early in the season, perhaps to pick up a fee.
annotation.walkthrough: Collect (stress on the first syllable) is a short prayer in church liturgy; possibly marks it as an example. The surface wants the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A collect is a short prayer read in church services.

entries.clue: Great supply of baked food served in a ball? (9)

indicators.note: BUN is placed inside A DANCE

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance
a bun is baked, placed after the A

annotation.surface: Plenty of pastries laid out at a grand ball.
annotation.walkthrough: Ball reads as something round like a bun; it is the formal dance.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the word comes from Latin for overflowing, a supply more than enough.

entries.clue: Foremost among Doctor’s adversaries: loathsome extraterrestrial killer? (5)

annotation.definition: Foremost among Doctor’s adversaries: loathsome extraterrestrial killer?

indicators.note: take the front letter of each following word

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

annotation.surface: A description of the Doctor's deadliest alien foe.
annotation.walkthrough: The Doctor is Doctor Who, the long-running British TV sci-fi hero, and the Daleks are his most famous enemies, murderous aliens. The whole clue both describes one and spells it.
annotation.definitionFit: Daleks are the chief alien adversaries of Doctor Who.

entries.clue: Eg Pavarotti’s general tendency (5)

blocks.note: Luciano Pavarotti, the Italian opera singer, as an example of his voice type
the general drift or course of a discussion

annotation.surface: A comment on Pavarotti's usual habits.
annotation.walkthrough: The possessive makes the two definitions read as one phrase; split it into Pavarotti and general tendency.
annotation.definitionFit: Pavarotti was a tenor, and tenor also means the general course or drift.

entries.clue: Interrogate cook (5)

annotation.surface: An order to question the chef.
annotation.walkthrough: Cook reads as a noun, the person to be questioned; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to interrogate them hard; to grill food is to cook it.

entries.clue: Obtain reassurance at last in test for infidelity (9)

indicators.note: take the last letter of reassurance
REACH and E go inside TRY

blocks.note: a try is a test or attempt
to reach = to obtain or attain

annotation.surface: Seeking comfort from a test for an unfaithful partner.
annotation.walkthrough: Test for infidelity reads as one thing; for is the link and test gives TRY.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: betrayal of faith, the breaking of trust that infidelity implies.

entries.clue: Make lace, a tangled mass (3)

blocks.note: knot thread with a shuttle to form lace
a rare noun sense: a matted tangle, as of hair

annotation.surface: Lacemaking that ends in a tangle.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition is a rare noun sense of tat, a tangled or matted mass.
annotation.definitionFit: To tat is to make lace by knotting thread with a shuttle.

entries.clue: Dull group losing leader in spinney (7)

indicators.note: the first letter of SET is dropped

annotation.surface: A dreary crowd who have lost their guide in a small wood.
annotation.walkthrough: A spinney is a small wood or copse, a British word.
annotation.definitionFit: A thicket is a dense group of bushes or trees, like a spinney.

entries.clue: Verbally inform deserters about communications satellite (7)

indicators.note: the spoken word TELL gives the sound TEL
about means turned around, so the word for deserters is read backwards

blocks.note: RATS (deserters, as in rats leaving a sinking ship) reversed

annotation.surface: Telling someone by word of mouth about defectors and a satellite.
annotation.walkthrough: Rats are proverbial deserters, leaving a sinking ship. TELL and TEL sound alike, so only the sound is taken.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the 1962 satellite that first relayed live television across the Atlantic.
